headline: New OpenSSH and musl flaw lets attackers bypass Linux passwords
summary: A newly disclosed vulnerability nicknamed sshole combines flaws in OpenSSH and musl-libc, letting attackers bypass password authentication on Alpine Linux and possibly other musl-based distros by entering an overly long password, over 256 characters per Tom's Hardware. The Register calls the underlying OpenSSH bug decade-old and now fixed.

claims.statement: A vulnerability nicknamed sshole combines OpenSSH and musl-libc flaws to bypass password authentication on Alpine Linux and possibly other distros.
